findings.explanation: The null assertion runs before dispatch and throws IllegalArgumentException with "Location must not be null". Registered ProtocolResolvers are held in a LinkedHashSet, so normal registration through addProtocolResolver is insertion-ordered and duplicate entries are suppressed. Each resolver runs before built-in routing; its first non-null Resource is returned, while null means continue. A leading slash is sent to the protected getResourceByPath hook. `classpath:` strips its prefix and constructs ClassPathResource; `classpath*:` constructs the nested DefaultResourceLoader.ClassPathAllResource. Otherwise the location is parsed as a URL: ResourceUtils.isFileURL recognizes `file`, `vfsfile`, and `vfs`, producing FileUrlResource; other valid URL protocols produce UrlResource. MalformedURLException falls back to getResourceByPath. In the unmodified loader, that hook constructs DefaultResourceLoader.ClassPathContextResource using the loader's ClassLoader. These branches only construct resource handles; they do not test existence or open content.

Both two-argument constructors reject a null path through Assert.notNull and clean it with StringUtils.cleanPath. The Class-based constructor retains the cleaned caller coordinate in `path`: with a non-null Class and no leading slash, `absolutePath` is prefixed with the class's package resource path, while a leading slash denotes classpath-absolute lookup and one leading slash is removed from `absolutePath`. It stores `classLoader` as null and stores the Class argument exactly; if that argument is null, no package is added and both lookup-context fields are null, leading later access to the system-resource branch. The ClassLoader-based constructor instead removes a leading slash after cleaning, stores that result as both `path` and `absolutePath`, stores no Class, and stores either the explicit loader or the result of ClassUtils.getDefaultClassLoader(). The one-argument constructor delegates to that ClassLoader overload with null. Spring's default selector prefers the thread context loader and has defining-loader/system fallbacks, but selection occurs when the handle is constructed; the handle does not dynamically select it again during later access. Likewise, DefaultResourceLoader resolves its current default before passing it into each newly created handle. `getPath()` exposes `absolutePath`, not necessarily the original Class-relative coordinate; `getClassLoader()` returns the Class's loader for a non-null Class or the stored loader otherwise. Cleaning is lexical normalization of separators and dot segments, not traversal prevention or a containment guarantee.

The shared resolver preserves the lookup API's coordinate rules: a stored Class receives the cleaned `path`, including its relative-versus-leading-slash meaning; a stored ClassLoader receives slashless `absolutePath`; and absence of both contexts uses ClassLoader.getSystemResource with `absolutePath`. An IllegalArgumentException from any branch is suppressed and represented as null. `exists()` simply tests whether resolveURL returns non-null, so a missing resource or suppressed IllegalArgumentException yields false. `getURL()` calls the same helper but throws FileNotFoundException when it gets null, otherwise returning the URL. Neither operation opens or retains a content stream, and getInputStream later performs a separate lookup, so successful existence or URL resolution does not establish that the subsequent stream lookup will succeed.

Stream access performs its own direct three-way dispatch: Class.getResourceAsStream receives `path`, ClassLoader.getResourceAsStream receives `absolutePath`, and the no-context case calls ClassLoader.getSystemResourceAsStream with `absolutePath`. A null result becomes FileNotFoundException; a non-null stream is returned unchanged. This method neither calls resolveURL nor inherits resolveURL's IllegalArgumentException suppression, and it performs no preliminary existence check. It does not close a successful stream or cache its content; ownership of the returned stream passes to the caller.

Ordinary ClassPathResource computes against its stored lookup coordinate `path`, then constructs another handle. StringUtils.applyRelativePath finds the final `/`, removes the final segment, and appends the relative argument; if the original has no separator, it returns the relative argument unchanged. A leading slash on the relative argument merely suppresses insertion of another separator: for example, `a/b` plus `/c` becomes `a/c`, not `/c`. With no original separator, `/c` remains `/c` and is then interpreted by the selected constructor. Construction runs cleanPath again, so dot segments introduced by the helper can be normalized. A non-null Class is preserved and keeps Class-relative semantics; otherwise the stored ClassLoader is passed to the ClassLoader constructor. Consequently, an original `(path, (Class<?>) null)` has no Class marker to preserve and its relative handle takes the ClassLoader constructor's null/default-selection path. The default loader's ClassPathContextResource differs by implementing ContextResource, returning `getPath()` from `getPathWithinContext()`, applying the helper to `getPath()`, and overriding createRelative to return another ClassPathContextResource, thereby preserving that subtype. All of this creates lexical handles only: it neither proves resource existence nor establishes a filesystem security boundary.
